role: Barwise's partial isomorphism relation (nonempty back and forth set of partial isomorphisms of partial substructures; function graphs only)
notes: Barwise 1974 Part I 10.1 p. 244. Same glyph as \(\cong_p\) in def:p03-w03-p03-039-partial-iso (Marker; partial embeddings preserving all atomic formulas); different underlying notion for function symbols.

role: equivalence of two L-structures for all sentences of L* (Barwise)
least ordinal bounding all Sigma-1-1 classes of ordinals of a logic
notes: Barwise 1974 Part II Definition 1.6 p. 252; strict reading of bounded by.

role: set of finite partial isomorphisms with m-level back and forth extensions
notes: Finite levels of Barwise's sequences I_beta (Theorem 10.5 p. 245); letter J chosen to avoid Barwise's I.

role: first-order level-m type formula recording relations and function graphs
notes: Replaces Barwise's sigma (p. 246) for languages with function symbols.

role: Barwise's beth function with beth_0(lambda)=lambda and beth_alpha=beth_alpha(0)
notes: Barwise 1974 Part I 10 p. 246. In this indexing beth_omega = aleph_0; differs from the P6 global beth hierarchy (registry row for \(\aleph_\alpha\),\(\beth_\alpha\)), which starts at aleph_0. Local to this chapter.

role: infinitary logic with formulas of fewer than kappa subformulas; with arbitrary set conjunctions
notes: Barwise 1974 p. 246: L_kappa-omega defined by |phi| < kappa (subformula count), not by the size of conjunctions.

role: cardinality of the set of subformulas; set of subformulas of an infinitary formula
notes: Barwise 1974 p. 246. Distinct from the P7 index operation sub_i.

role: transfinite continuation of the sets J_m (intersection at limits)
notes: Barwise's I_beta of Theorem 10.5 p. 245 for finite partial isomorphisms.

role: set of level-beta type formulas in n free variables
distinguished universe predicate in Barwise languages
notes: Always belongs to a language; interpreted by the entire universe; an interpretation may replace it with a relativizing predicate.

role: category of languages and interpretations in Barwise 1974
notes: Five category conditions stated locally; not a class of models.

role: pulled-back partial structure and its universe
notes: Pull-back along a k-term interpretation; invertible means that the pulled-back functions are total, including constants.

role: sentence class, functor map, translated sentence and least occurrence language
notes: Barwise logic syntax; functor preserves identity and composition.
